summary:
Aceh operates under a separate Sharia criminal code (Qanun No. 6/2014) that criminalises same-sex conduct as liwath and musahaqah with penalties of up to 100 lashes or eight years' imprisonment—none of which exists in any other Indonesian province. Enforcement by Wilayatul Hisbah Sharia police and Satpol PP is active and escalating: in February 2025 two men caught in a boarding house received a combined 159 lashes publicly in Banda Aceh for consensual sex (one collapsed at the end), and in August 2025 two men received 80 lashes each for hugging and kissing, with the net widening beyond sex to non-sexual contact. A boarding-house raid in February 2025 specifically detained a waria (transfeminine person) alongside a gay student, and in January 2018 police detained and forcibly shaved twelve transwomen.

Deviation from the national score (0.15) is −0.12, the largest single-province gap on this map. A visitor with no criminal conduct elsewhere in Indonesia can be caned in Aceh for the same private behaviour. The Qanun does not name waria explicitly, but the Feb 2025 raid shows enforcement reaches them. No other unit in this country carries an active corporal-punishment regime for consensual adult conduct.

This sits well below West Java (0.08), where the threat is vigilante mob violence with police inaction rather than a codified sentencing framework. Aceh's risk is state-imposed and judicially formalised: Islamic Shariah District Courts hand down caning sentences publicly, sometimes behind closed doors, and the punishment is carried out on a stage in a city park before crowds.

sources.summary: QURU' Journal of Family Law and Culture study (2025), 'The Increasing Number of Waria in Banda Aceh: Between Social Challenges and Law Enforcement': empirical-legal study of how Qanun No. 6 of 2014 on jinayat (liwath, musahaqah, khalwat) is enforced against waria, confirming that Aceh's special Sharia authority includes caning (uqubat cambuk) applied where a violation occurs and that enforcement pressure falls on visible gender nonconformity.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time; the underlying CNN report (27 Feb 2025) covers two men publicly caned a combined 159 strokes in Banda Aceh after being caught by residents in a boarding house; one collapsed at the end of the punishment and was carried off by Sharia police.

CBS News/AP report (26 Aug 2025): two men aged 20 and 21 were publicly caned 80 strokes each in Banda Aceh's Bustanussalatin park after an Islamic Shariah court convicted them of hugging and kissing (ruled as leading to banned sexual relations), before ~100 spectators, with eight more people caned the same day; notes Aceh permits up to 100 lashes for morality offences (gay sex, unmarried sex, gambling, drinking, women's 'tight' clothing) and that the trial itself was held behind closed doors; Amnesty called it 'state-sanctioned discrimination and cruelty'.

Portal Aceh/iNews report (18 Feb 2025): Banda Aceh Satpol PP and Wilayatul Hisbah detained a pair — a waria and a gay university student — in a boarding-house room; the enforcement unit's Sharia-law enforcement division head confirmed they face up to 100 caning strokes under the Qanun liwath provision and urged kos-house owners to police tenants, showing boarding-house round-ups on this basis are recurring and that waria are swept up in liwath enforcement.

Australian Human Rights Institute (UNSW) commentary: transgender women are the most frequent victims of police violence in Indonesia's anti-LGBT upturn; records the January 2018 case where Aceh police detained twelve transwomen and forcibly shaved/cut their hair to teach them 'how to act like real men', within a national pattern of state failure to protect trans citizens.
